rv.q: Paired with an exemplary story, very fine acting and discerning sure direction, Citadel’s production of I and You is a delight that can be savored long after the lights come up.
I AND YOU leaves us with this important life lesson.
What is “divine” is Citadel’s production of “I and You.”
I and You is a beautiful and touching piece—a reminder of the power of connection, the fragility of life, and the enduring impact of great storytelling.
It was amazing! Better yet…it's a masterpiece.
It's an ending that leaves you breathless — and in that moment, you realize the true power of humanity: connected to something much bigger than ourselves.
The play is quite heartwarming and the two actors have created characters that appear to be real and could easily be the boy and girl next door.
Before you see the show, and you should absolutely go, know that Whitman was a 19th century American poet...
So my recommendation would be, if you’re not a fan of shows that are mostly dialogue that you need to sift through, this might not be the show for you.

cn.t: Critics praise this intimate two-hander for its emotional depth and surprise ending, with Gunderson's script and strong performances earning enthusiastic recommendations across the board.
